clips.title: The story
paras: A grim necessity of undead existence in Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken must scavenge animal hides to replace their decaying flesh. Shelene Rhobart tasks adventurers with gathering darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin to patch damaged bodies.

Forsaken flesh does not heal naturally. Sustaining physical wounds leaves rotting gaps that cannot regenerate through normal biological means. To maintain their forms and keep their corpses functional, the Forsaken must source organic material from the living world and stitch replacement pieces over their injuries.

Not every hide serves the same anatomical purpose. Thick darkhound hide offers durability for broad, sturdy repairs. Delicate duskbat wing membranes are light and pliable enough to cover faces and fingers without creating stiff, clumsy layers. Meanwhile, the pliable skin of Vile Fin murlocs is gathered to line internal membranes and sensitive areas such as inner cheeks and mouths.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: One part of undeath no one mentions is what happens when we are injured. How does the skin of an undead heal itself?
Ours is a cursed life, friend. We must take from the living to further our own existence.
When we sustain an injury, we must replace our skin which usually means animal hides. Since different hide thicknesses are better for different places on our bodies a variety is key!
Bring me wing membranes of a duskbat, hides from a darkhound and skin of a Vile Fin murloc.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Have you gathered the skin I inquired about? Our stocks are running low.
It may seem odd to ask for murloc skin but it works well for internal membranes, or surfaces like cheeks or mouths.
Similarly, the duskbat wing membranes are especially suited for more delicate areas, like faces or fingers. It prevents the skin from being too... Thick.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah, excellent! Thank you for acquiring these. I can promise they will be put to good use.
